# Volume 3 — Chapter XXIV Enter Ezra

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“PROSPECT POINT, “August 20th.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0000 }

“Dear Nell—spelled—with—an—E,” Cressy penned, “I have to force my eyes to stay open just to send you a note. Honey, I’ve ignored you terribly over the course of this summer, yet I have ignored every one of my other correspondents as well. There is a giant stack of letters awaiting my reply, which means I have to pull myself together mentally and get to work. Please forgive my jumbled metaphors. I am terribly drowsy. Yesterday evening Cousin Emily and I paid a visit to a neighbor. A few other guests were present as well, and the moment those unlucky individuals departed, our hostess alongside her trio of daughters ripped every single one of them to shreds. I was certain they would start picking apart Cousin Emily and me the instant the door was closed after our departure. Upon our return home, Mrs. Lilly let us know that the previously mentioned neighbor’s farmhand was suspected of coming down with scarlet fever. One can consistently rely on Mrs. Lilly for uplifting news of that sort. I am terrified of scarlet fever. Once I got into bed, thoughts of it kept me from falling asleep. I tossed and turned continuously, suffering through terrifying dreams whenever I managed to nod off for a brief moment; then at three o'clock I woke up suffering from a high fever, a raw throat, and a violent headache. I was certain I was sick with scarlet fever; I leaped out of bed in a fright and searched for Cousin Emily’s ‘doctor book’ so I could study the symptoms. Nell, I possessed every single one of them. Therefore I returned to bed, and having learned the worst, slept soundly for the remainder of the night. Even though I have never been able to comprehend why a top would sleep more soundly than any other object. However, when I woke up this morning I felt entirely fine, meaning it could not have been the fever after all. I reckon that even if I contracted it yesterday evening, it would not have manifested that quickly. I am capable of keeping that in mind during the day, but at three in the morning I am simply incapable of reasoning logically.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0001 }

“I guess you are curious about my presence at Prospect Point. You see, I am fond of spending one summer month by the seaside, and father demands my attendance at the ‘select boardinghouse’ owned by his second-cousin Emily at Prospect Point. Therefore, two weeks back, I arrived as I always do. And in accordance with routine, elderly ‘Uncle Mark Miller’ drove me from the depot using his antique buggy and the creature he describes as his ‘generous purpose’ horse. He is a pleasant aged fellow who presented me with a few pink peppermints. To me, peppermints have a distinctively holy quality—likely because Grandmother Lindsay habitually handed them to me during services when I was small. On one occasion, alluding to the scent of peppermints, I inquired, ‘Is that the odor of sanctity?’ I hesitated to consume Uncle Mark’s peppermints owing to the fact that he merely retrieved them loose from his coat, needing to sort out some corroded nails and additional items from the batch prior to handing them over. However, refusing to wound his precious old emotions under any circumstances, I cautiously scattered them piece by piece along the thoroughfare. After I had discarded the final piece, Uncle Mark remarked, with mild disapproval, ‘Ye shouldn’t a’et all them candies to onct, Miss Cressy. You’ll likely have the stummick-ache.’
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0002 }

“Except for me, Cousin Emily entertains merely five roomers—a single young man alongside four aged women. Mrs. Lilly sits to my right side. She belongs to that class of individuals who appear to derive a morbid delight from describing every single one of their numerous sicknesses, pains, and aches. It is impossible to name a single malady without her uttering, while her head shakes, “Ah, I know too well what that is”—after which every detail is dumped upon you. Ezra asserts that he formerly brought up locomotor ataxia where she could hear, whereupon she claimed she was all too familiar with that condition. It plagued her for a decade before a wandering physician at last healed her.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0003 }

“Who is Ezra? Just wait, Nell Harcourt. You shall be told everything regarding Ezra when the correct time and place arrive. He must not be confused with respectable old women.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0004 }

“Mrs. Phinney sits next to me on my left at the table. A lamenting, sorrowful tone marks her speech constantly—you feel a tense anticipation that she will break down weeping at any second. The way she presents herself suggests that existence is truly a valley of grief to her, and that smiling, to say nothing of laughing, constitutes a genuinely blameworthy weakness. Her judgment of me is harsher than Aunt Euphemia's, and she lacks the deep affection to compensate for it that Aunty J. possesses.”
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0005 }

“Directly opposite and to one side of me sits Miss Maria Grimsby. On my very first day here, I mentioned to Miss Maria that rain appeared somewhat likely—and Miss Maria laughed. I observed that the way from the train station was quite lovely—and Miss Maria laughed. I noted that a handful of mosquitoes still seemed to remain—and Miss Maria laughed. I stated that Prospect Point retained all its former beauty—and Miss Maria laughed. Were I to state to Miss Maria, ‘My father has hanged himself, my mother has taken poison, my brother is in the penitentiary, and I am in the last stages of consumption,’ Miss Maria would laugh. It is beyond her control—she came into the world this way; nevertheless, it is deeply gloomy and dreadful.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0006 }

“Mrs. Hollis is the fifth old lady. She is a sweet old person; however, she is a most uninteresting conversationalist because she speaks only well of everyone.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0007 }

“And at this moment regarding Ezra, Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0008 }

“On my very first day there, I observed a youth seated across the table from me, beaming in my direction like someone who had been acquainted with me since my infancy. Because Uncle Mark had informed me, I was aware that Ezra Hale was his name, that he was studying theology at St. Columbia, and that he had assumed responsibility for the Point Prospect Mission Church over the summer.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0009 }

“He is an extremely unattractive young man—honestly, the most unattractive young man I have ever laid eyes on. He possesses a large, gangly frame featuring ridiculous, elongated legs. His hair is flaxen and limp, his eyes are green, his mouth is large, and his ears—though I refrain from considering his ears whenever possible.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0010 }

“His voice is delightful—closing your eyes makes him charming—and the beauty of his soul and nature is unquestionable.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0011 }

“We became close friends immediately. Naturally, he graduated from Wexcombe, which serves as a bond between us. We went fishing and boating with each other; additionally, we strolled along the shore in the moonlight. In the moonlight he appeared less plain, and oh, he was delightful. Delightfulness virtually radiated from him. The elderly women—with the exception of Mrs. Hollis—disapprove of Ezra, since he laughs and jokes—and since he clearly prefers the company of silly me to theirs.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0012 }

“Somehow, Nell, I do not wish for him to regard me as shallow. This makes no sense. Why ought I to be concerned about the opinion of a flaxen-haired individual named Ezra, whom I had not previously set eyes on?
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0013 }

“On the previous Sunday, Ezra gave the sermon at the church in the village. Naturally, I attended, yet I was unable to grasp that Ezra was about to preach. To me, it continued to feel like an enormous joke that he was a minister—or was preparing to become one.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0014 }

“Well, Ezra preached. And, once he had been preaching for ten minutes, I felt so tiny and meaningless that I believed I had to be unseen by the unassisted eye. Ezra didn't say a single thing regarding women, and he didn't look my way once. Even so, right then, I understood what an awful, trivial, shallow-spirited little butterfly I was, and the dreadful extent to which I must diverge from the woman of Ezra’ ideals. That woman would be magnificent, powerful, and honorable. He was exceptionally serious, gentle, and faithful. He embodied all that a clergyman should be. I marvelled at how I had ever considered him unattractive—yet he truly is!—what with those impassioned eyes and that scholarly forehead that his unkempt hair concealed on ordinary days.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0015 }

“The sermon was splendid, allowing me to listen to it for eternity, yet it caused me to feel completely miserable. Oh, how I desire to resemble you, Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0016 }

“Overtaking me along the path toward home, he smiled with his customary brightness. Yet his expression was no longer able to fool me. The true Ezra had been revealed to me. It made me ponder whether he would ever behold the true Cressy—a person whom no one, not even you, Nell, has yet beheld.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0017 }

“‘Ezra,’ I uttered—omitting to address him as Mr. Hale. Was it not terrible? Yet during certain moments such details are irrelevant—‘Ezra, being a minister was your destiny from birth. It was impossible for you to be anything different.’
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0018 }

“‘No, I was unable to,’ he stated with gravity. ‘I attempted to be a different person for a extended period—I lacked the desire to be a clergyman. However, I eventually realized that it was the labor assigned to me—and with the assistance of God, I will endeavor to fulfill it.’
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0019 }

“He spoke in a quiet, respectful tone. It occurred to me that he would perform his labor effectively and with noble purpose; a woman possessing the inherent disposition and preparation to assist his efforts would be fortunate indeed. She would not resemble a feather, tossed by each changing breeze of whim. Knowing which hat to wear would never be an issue for her. Likely, a single one would be all she owned. Clergymen are rarely wealthy. Yet, owning merely one hat, or even none, would not bother her, for Ezra would be hers.
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0020 }

“Nell Harcourt, do not dare to utter, suggest, or entertain the thought that Mr. Hale has won my heart. How could I ever harbor feelings for an awkward, impoverished, unattractive theology student—with the name Ezra? In the words of Uncle Mark, ‘It’s impossible, and what’s more it’s improbable.’
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0021 }

“Good night, CRESSY.”
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0022 }

“P.S. Although it cannot be—I am dreadfully fearful that it is real. I feel joyful, miserable, and frightened. It is impossible for him to ever love me, I am certain. Is it possible that I might grow into a decent minister’s wife, Nell? Furthermore, will I be expected to guide the prayers? P G.”
{: #nw-v03-c24-p0023 }
